# DTSA 5304
CU Boulder MSDS Fundamentals of Data Visualization (DTSA 5304) Final Project

## Assignment Information and Repository Structure

This repository contains my final assignment for DTSA 5304 as well as the code to reproduce all analyses.

* `rise_of_cs.qmd` is the project's main file. It contains the code for all visualizations, background information about the dataset and project, and a narrative about design decisions.  
* `rise_of_cs.html` is the rendered version of `rise_of_cs.qmd` and will be submitted for grading. It can be regenerated by following the instructions below (please note that `.html` output has been excluded from version control). However, for convenience, it is also available via Posit Connect Cloud:
    + **[Final HTML report](TODO_add_link.com)**
* `survey.qmd` reproduces the visualizations from the main report for sharing with evaluation participants (`rise_of_cs.qmd` saves its output in the `plots/` directory). To share this document with survey takers, it has been made available on Posit Connect Cloud: 
    + **[Evaluation survey](https://01a0b9b8-dc14-b9e3-1698-efb1d148ea39.share.connect.posit.cloud/)**
* `src/` contains Python scripts for extracting, transforming, and loading the 
Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS). These scripts are called by `rise_of_cs.qmd`.


## Reproducibility and Environment Setup

This project uses `uv` to manage dependencies and create a virtual environment for reproducible analyses. To reproduce the final report:

1. Clone the repository, optionally specifying a specific location to clone to, replacing `<target-folder-name>` with a directory such as `~/Downloads/treys_dtsa5304`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/treyhendrix/dtsa5304.git <target-folder-name>
```

2. Install the `uv` and `quarto` tools if you do not already have them installed

* [uv official installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* Once you have `uv` installed, you can install Quarto (if you do not already have it) using: 

```bash
uv tool install quarto-cli
```

3. Navigate to the cloned directory and create a virtual environment by running:

```bash
uv sync
```

4. Render `rise_of_cs.qmd` and reproduce the final HTML report by running the command below: 

```bash
uv run quarto render rise_of_cs.qmd
```

5. Render `survey.qmd` after the previous step populated the `plots` directory to reproduce the survey HTML document:

```bash
uv run quarto render survey.qmd
```
